# Negative-offset top-and-bottom wrapping recovery

Original XML/OPC and PNG controls generated by
`tools/negative_wrap_recovery_fixture.py`, using Python's standard library and
original fixture builders. No corpus artwork or third-party document engine is
included. Each unsupported/matched pair differs only in the two affected
pictures' wrapping (`wrapTopAndBottom` versus `wrapNone`). Signed offsets,
geometry, source text, supported positive-offset wrapping and tables are equal.

The three pairs put the failure in body, header or footer content. Two failing
pictures surround healthy content: one extends across its anchor and one lies
entirely above it. Body and story tables, healthy text and positive-offset
wrapping must survive. The original body case fell back to plain text with no
decoded assets, floating objects or tables.

The read-only approximation retains each affected picture at its signed
position but omits its text wrapping. This can overlap text and change
pagination. The banner explicitly says so, identifies each affected paragraph
and drawing, and includes the story part when applicable. Healthy drawing
wrapping stays active. The source model and package are not modified; downloads
remain byte-identical. Editing remains disabled for the unsupported sources.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.12 and 20.4.3.3 specify positioning offsets;
§20.4.2.20 specifies top-and-bottom wrapping; §20.4.2.15 describes the no-wrap
behavior used only for this disclosed display approximation. This is not full
support for negative-offset wrapping or evidence of a reference/spec divergence.
Native layout support, including effects on preceding text, remains open.

Browser tests compare complete page pixels and body/story geometry at 75% and
100%, verify the visible explanation, reject edits and preserve original bytes.
Unit tests verify strict rejection, local recovery, unchanged source models,
healthy-object identity and propagation of unrelated measurement failures.
